name: Learn basic fishing knots
blurb: Four knots cover almost all fishing: a hook knot, a loop, a line-to-line join and a leader connection. Monofilament is unforgiving, so technique and lubrication matter more than with rope.
gear: Practice hooks with the points cut off, or swivels
steps: Learn the improved clinch knot for tying line to hook or swivel — the everyday workhorse.
Learn the palomar knot, which is stronger, simpler and works well with braid.
Learn the double surgeon’s knot or blood knot for joining two lines.
Learn a loop knot — the non-slip mono loop — so lures can swing freely.
Always wet the knot before tightening: friction heat weakens monofilament dramatically.
Test each knot by pulling it to failure and noticing whether the line breaks at the knot or elsewhere.
tips: Tighten slowly and evenly. A jerked knot fails at the worst moment.
Trim tags close but not flush, and check knots after every snag.
proof: You tie all four in the field, in the cold, and none fails under load during a session.
